symptom: Over --mcp, `create microflow M.X ($T: System.UserType) begin … end;` fails: `ped_create_document … {"/parameters/0/entity":"Reference with qualified name System.UserType of type DomainModels$Entity not found."}`. A module enumeration (`Rules.RuleResult`) works. On the local engines the same script reports success and DESCRIBE prints a plausible bare `$T: System.UserType`, but mx check gives `[CE1613] "The selected entity 'System.UserType' no longer exists."` for the parameter and for a `returns System.DeviceType`. The explicit `$T: enum System.UserType` (what DESCRIBE emits for an enumeration) was refused: "enumeration 'System.UserType' not found for parameter 'T'"
cause: The visitor types every bare qualified name in a flow parameter or return position as TypeEntity. buildMicroflowFromStmt / buildNanoflowFromStmt / execCreateRule fall back from entity to enumeration only after the entity lookup misses, and skip that lookup entirely for the System module (isBuiltinModuleEntity: its entities are not stored in the project), so a System enumeration kept the entity guess and was written as DataTypes$ObjectType with Entity "System.UserType". The explicit form failed separately: findEnumeration reads ListEnumerations, which never contains the System module's enumerations
fix: settleSystemEnumeration retypes a TypeEntity whose qualified name is in meta.SystemEnumerations to TypeEnumeration before validation, at all six sites (microflow, nanoflow, rule × parameter, return type); isKnownEnumeration accepts a System enumeration where findEnumeration cannot see it. A System entity (System.User) stays an object type
insight: It was never an MCP bug: the local engines wrote the same wrong object type and only mx check (CE1613) noticed; MCP surfaced it because PED resolves references at write time. DESCRIBE hid it — it renders an enumeration type as `enum X` and an object type as bare `X`, so a bare `System.UserType` in describe output IS the symptom, not proof of a correct write. Dump the stored DataTypes$*Type (`mxcli bson dump --type microflow`) rather than reading describe. The general lesson for references into System: 'do not judge what you cannot list' covers existence, not kind — whether a name is an entity or an enumeration changes the stored shape, so it must still be decided, and modelsdk/meta.SystemEnumerations is the list to decide it from. Verified live over --mcp on Studio Pro 11.15.0-rc.4 (ped_read_document reads back DataTypes$EnumerationType for parameter and return type), with a stubbed-fix control reproducing the PED error
